correctness.rationale: Niu\'s Theorem A identifies the extendable group with \(H\cap\operatorname{Stab}(\Gamma_\mu(J)\cdot[a])\), and \(\Gamma_\mu(J)\subset\{\pm1\}\) contains \(+1\). The sign homomorphism on the setwise stabilizer has kernel the oriented-class stabilizer; a hyperelliptic involution acts by \(-I\), lies in \(H\) because it is the identity modulo \(2\), and supplies an order-two splitting. For odd \(p\), squared Dehn twists lie in \(H\) and realize all mod-\(p\) symplectic transvection coefficients. These transvections are transitive on nonzero homology classes, yielding finite orbit sizes \(p^{2g}-1\) and \((p^{2g}-1)/2\). The subgroup-index inequalities follow because integral stabilizers lie inside the corresponding mod-\(p\) stabilizers.

value.rationale: The source establishes qualitative infinite index. The accepted theorem adds two concrete structural layers: it quantifies the only knot-exterior sign ambiguity as an exact split \(C_2\), and it turns infinite-index nonextendability into explicit finite congruence tests of sizes \(p^{2g}-1\) or \((p^{2g}-1)/2\). These finite actions give practical certificates that a mapping class cannot extend and expose a clean difference between longitude-rigid and longitude-reversible knots without changing the rim-surgery construction.
